anglicized_name: Keshavnarayana Chok, Keshav Narayan Chowk, Patan Museum
description_en: The origins of Keśavanārāyaṇa Coka are shrouded in mystery but it is believed that the palace building replaced an earlier monastery. The monastery was relocated to Hakha Bāhāḥ (LAL0390) and this move is still commemorated every year when an image of Akṣobhya Buddha is placed in a copper pot of water in front of the palace's golden door. For one month, the public worships the image recalling the sanctity of the site. The courtyard building was probably established by Siddhinarasiṃha Malla as Caukoṭa in 1627, reshaped in 1674 and rebuilt again in 1734 by Vishnu Malla as a fort with four towers. The three-story building has undergone many renovations and alterations over the past centuries with the upper story and roofs rebuilt after the 1934 earthquake and again in the late 1980s and 1990s. Today, only two of the towers remain, both rebuilt after they were seriously damaged in the 1934 earthquake. The east-wing collapsed in 1934 and was haphazardly rebuilt with recycled materials. It was again rebuilt in the early 1990s as a partly modern building in a hybrid style employing both Malla and Rana era design elements.The entrance of the courtyard is flanked by two stone lions. The golden door is surmounted with a gilttoraṇawhichwas offered by Jaṅga Bahādura in 1854. The golden window of the second floor, calledlũjhyāis made of gilt copper repousse. A statue of Sṛṣṭikāntā Lokeśvara is located in the enter of the window. A statue of Śani is installed on top of the west wing roof.Following the end of Malla rule in 1768, the building was used for various administrative purposes and in the 1950s was adapted to house a school. In the early 1980s parts of the west and north wings were turned into a small museum. From 1984-1997 the palace was renovated from ground up and converted into the Patan Museum with funds provided by the Austrian and Nepali Governments. In 1994, the north-east wing was restored in-situ and today it houses temporary exhibition galleries and guest studios.
description_ne: पाटन दरबार क्षेत्रभित्र रहेका अनेक चोकहरूमध्ये केशवनारायण चोक पनि एक हो । यो चोक पाटनको प्रसिद्ध कृष्णमन्दिरको ठिक अगाडि अवस्थित छ । चोकमा प्रवेश गर्ने मुख्य ढोका र त्यसमाथिको तोरण सुनको जलप लगाइएको पाताले मोडी सजाइएको छ जुन सन् १८५४ मा जंगबहादुर राणाको पालामा बनेको हो । मूल ढोका दायाँ–बायाँ एक जोडा सिंहमूर्ति स्थिपित छन् । यस ढोकाको ठिक माथि दोस्रो तलामा कलात्मक झ्याल रहेको छ । झ्यालको मध्य भागलाई तामाको पाताले मोडी त्यसमा सुनको जलप लगाइएको छ । सुनौलो झ्याल भएकाले यसलाई ''लुँझ्याः'' भनिन्छ । सुनौलो झ्यालको केन्द्र भागमा सृष्टिकान्ता लोकेश्वरको मूर्ति छ भने उनको दायाँ-बायाँ स-साना अन्य मूर्तिहरू देखिन्छन् । यस झ्यालको ठिक माथि छानामा शनिदेवको धातुमूर्ति रहेको छ । चोकको बीच भागमा केशवनारायण मन्दिर अवस्थित छ । यही मन्दिरको नामबाट यो चोकको नाम रहन गएको हो । पाटनमा महापात्रहरूको शासनकाल (सन् ११४४–१५९७) मा उनीहरूबाट निर्माण भएका कीर्तिहरूमध्ये केशवनारायण मन्दिर पनि एक हो (Gutschow, 2011, 307) । गुम्बज शैलीको मन्दिरभित्र नारायण सहित गरुड र लक्ष्मीको मूर्ति रहेको छ । मन्दिरभित्र कृष्ण र उनका दुई पत्नीहरूकोको खण्डित मूर्ति पनि रहेको छ । चोकको दक्षिण-पश्चिम कुनामा संवत् ६७ को नरेन्द्रदेवको अभिलेख खडा छ । सम्भवतः यस चोकलाइ चौकोटको रूप दिने कार्य सिद्धिनरसिंह मल्लले सन् १६२७ मा गरेका थिए (Gutschow, 2011, 318) । हाल चौकोटमध्ये पश्चिमी मोहोडामाथि दुई कोट (टावर) अवशेषका रूपमा रहेका छन् । यस चोकलाई घेरिएको चतुष्कोणाकार भवनको पहिलो र दोस्रो तला सन् १९५७ देखि संग्राहलयको रूपमा प्रयोग गरिएको छ ।मूल चोकको नजिकै रहेको चोकमा पहिला हख बाहाः थियो र पछि दरबार विस्तारको क्रममा सिद्धिनरसिंहले गाःबाहाः नजिकै स्थानान्तरण गरेको कुरा नेपालिकभूपवंशावली (19.3.10) मा उल्लेख छ । मूल चोकको नजिकै उत्तरपट्टि सुन्दरी चोक र त्यसको उत्तरपट्टि केशवनारायण चोक रहेको छ । केशवनारायण चोकको मुख्य द्वारअगाडि गुँला महिनामा बुद्धको मूर्ति प्रदर्शनमा राख्ने परम्परा हुनुका साथै चोकमा सम्यक् पर्वको समय फूद्यः (दीपङ्कर बुद्धका प्रतिनिधि) प्ररिक्रमा गराउन ल्याउने परम्परा भएबाट हख विहार सुन्दरी चोक र यो विहारको परिसरमा थियो भन्ने अन्दाज गर्न सकिन्छ ।

historical_events.event_description: A Licchavi inscription stands at the south-western corner of the courtyard. The subject matter of the inscription is not related to this courtyard. The inscription mentions that King Narendradeva transferred some of the rights to people.

At the main entrance to the courtyard, a golden gate was offered by Jaṅga Bahādura Rāṇā. The inscription mentions that the golden gate costmoha rū3,212. Some of the money was raised from selling an old gilt pinnacle, a bell and copper pots.

On the occasion of the coronation of King Mahendra, a beautification programme resulted in the corrugated sheet iron roofing being replaced by large sized British style roof tiles. The masonry surface of the coka was covered with cement plaster. The work was supported by His Majesty's Government of Nepal.

The north wing as restored with funding from the Austrian Development Agency; the Federal Ministry, Republic of Austria; Federal Chancellery of Austria; The University of Applied Arts, Vienna; and the Nepal Reconstruction Authority, Government of Nepal.
Following the 2015 earthquakes the galleries in the north, west and south wings were relocated to the north-east wing in order to allow the restoration of the damaged sections of the building.
The west wing was restored with funding from the Nepal Reconstruction Authority.
The Patan Museum was inaugurated by King Vīrendra Śāha. The inscription is embedded in a wall of the east-wingdalan.

historical_events.event_name: Restoration and establishment of the Patan Museum
historical_events.event_description: Between 1982 and 2000 the Keśavanārāyaṇa Coka was restored and converted into the Patan Museum.
